item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Monday
item.description: Government delays language tests for citizenship by a year, leader of Swedish Armed Forces calls for European nuclear deterrent, and other news from Sweden on Monday.

item.title: TELL US: What is the best district for foreigners in Stockholm?
item.description: From upmarket Östermalm and Nacka to more socially mixed areas like Bredäng or Kista, Stockholm has a huge number of different districts to choose from. We want to hear from readers about which is best for foreigners.

item.title: Do you have a teenage child who faces deportation from Sweden?
item.description: The campaign to end Sweden's teen deportation problem has had a breakthrough, with a real prospect of government action. We want to speak to those affected so we can bring it greater public attention. Get in touch if your child is at risk.

item.title: Swedish government delays language tests for citizenship by a year
item.description: Sweden's government has delayed the launch of the first language test for citizenship for over a year after Stockholm University, which was responsible for developing the test, said it could not have it ready in time.

item.title: Sweden pushes ahead with proposed law to tighten up citizenship
item.description: The Swedish government has revealed the details of a new law designed to tighten up citizenship requirements, among other things demanding an eight-year residency period and a 20,000 kronor self-sufficiency requirement.

item.title: 'People in Sweden are really raising their voices now and it’s very beautiful'
item.description: Annika Hirvonen, the immigration spokesperson for the Green Party, tells The Local that now the issue of teen deportations has shot to the top of the political agenda in Sweden, she is more and more hopeful that the law might be changed.

item.title: Will my Swedish citizenship application be rejected due to a test which doesn’t exist yet?
item.description: The Swedish government has now confirmed that any citizenship application not concluded by June 6th risks being processed under the new rules and rejected. But with tests not ready until next autumn, what does that mean for those of us who have already applied?

item.title: Q&A: Your questions about Sweden's new citizenship law
item.description: Sweden's government announced more details of its new citizenship law on February 9th, which left our readers with a lot of questions. We've tried to find some answers.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: medborgare
item.description: This word has been in the news a lot this week, as Sweden moved one step closer to tightening up rules for citizenship – but where does it come from?

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
item.description: Liberal Party calls for 'urgent' exemption clause to stop teen deportations, Norrlandsströmming herring gets EU protected origin status, and other news from Sweden on Tuesday.
